prompt:
Goal: Create a sophisticated cinematic editorial travel-magazine cover depicting an idealized, dreamlike view of Russia.

Canvas: Vertical magazine cover composition, 4:5 aspect ratio, elegant fine-art travel editorial aesthetic, soft cream paper texture, faint border lines near the edges, subtle translucent circular graphic accents in the upper-left and lower-right corners.

Layout: Place the cover title centered at the top in large widely spaced refined serif capitals reading RUSSIA. Beneath it, add a smaller elegant subtitle reading A VISUAL PORTRAIT OF RUSSIA. Add a tiny issue line below the subtitle reading No. 21 — 2026. Keep typography minimal, airy, and premium.

Scene: In the foreground, show a calm glass-like river filling the lower half of the image, reflecting the cityscape with gentle natural ripples. Add a few soft reeds and wild plants at the bottom-left edge for depth. On the right side, feature iconic Russian architecture inspired by Saint Basil’s Cathedral and the Kremlin: colorful onion domes, ornate red-brick towers, gold crosses, a tall clock tower, and a star-topped spire. Include exactly 2 main architectural groups: 1 ornate cathedral cluster with multiple domes and 1 Kremlin-style clock tower complex. On the left and center background, include a graceful stone bridge crossing the river, pale historic city buildings, misty tree-covered hills, and distant snow-capped mountains rising behind the city.

Lighting and atmosphere: Dreamy sunrise or sunset glow, pastel peach and pale blue sky, soft mist in the valleys, warm golden highlights on architecture and trees, atmospheric depth, serene romantic mood. The river reflection should mirror the cathedral, towers, bridge, trees, sky, and mountains, slightly blurred by ripples.

Visual style: Cinematic editorial travel poster, painterly photorealism, luxurious magazine cover, delicate color grading, realistic perspective, high detail, soft haze, elegant composition, no harsh contrast.

Constraints: Do not add people as main subjects; only tiny distant pedestrians may appear along the embankment. Keep the cover uncluttered, preserve negative space around the title, avoid modern skyscrapers, cars, logos, barcodes, extra captions, or watermarks.
